content.text:
Here are the findings:

---

**1. Provider abstraction -- `internal/idp/idp.go`**

File: `/bench/home/work/internal/idp/idp.go`

There is no Go `interface` defined in this package. Instead, the abstraction is a **plain data struct**:

```go
// lines 3-8
type IdentityProviderUserInfo struct {
    Identifier  string
    DisplayName string
    Email       string
    AvatarURL   string
}
```

This struct (defined at **line 3**) serves as the shared contract between any IDP implementation and the rest of the application. Any concrete provider is expected to return an `*idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo` from its `UserInfo` method. The coupling is structural/duck-typed rather than via an explicit `interface`.

---

**2. Concrete protocol implementation -- `internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`**

File: `/bench/home/work/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`

The concrete protocol is **OAuth2**. The implementation struct is:

```go
// lines 19-22
type IdentityProvider struct {
    config *storepb.OAuth2Config
}
```

Defined at **line 20**, this struct lives in package `oauth2` and wraps a protobuf-generated `OAuth2Config`. It exposes two methods:

- `ExchangeToken` (line 47) -- exchanges an authorization code for an access token (with optional PKCE support via `code_verifier`).
- `UserInfo` (line 83) -- fetches user info from the provider's userinfo endpoint using a Bearer token and returns an `*idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo`.

The constructor `NewIdentityProvider` (line 27) validates required config fields (`clientId`, `clientSecret`, `tokenUrl`, `userInfoUrl`, `fieldMapping.identifier`).

---

**Summary**

| Item | File | Line | Name |
|---|---|---|---|
| Abstraction (shared data type) | `/bench/home/work/internal/idp/idp.go` | 3 | `IdentityProviderUserInfo` struct |
| Concrete implementation | `/bench/home/work/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go` | 20 | `IdentityProvider` struct (OAuth2) |
| Constructor | `/bench/home/work/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go` | 27 | `NewIdentityProvider` |
| Token exchange method | `/bench/home/work/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go` | 47 | `ExchangeToken` |
| User info method | `/bench/home/work/internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go` | 83 | `UserInfo` |

The only concrete protocol that ships is **OAuth2**. There is no SAML or OIDC implementation in this codebase. The "provider abstraction" is convention-based (returning `*idp.IdentityProviderUserInfo`) rather than enforced by a Go `interface`.
